findings.title: isinstance check never matches spawn processes so unhealthy flushers are never killed
findings.body: Processes are created with `self.mp_context.Process` where `mp_context` is `multiprocessing.get_context('spawn')`, i.e. `SpawnProcess` instances. Both `_ensure_processes_alive` and `join` guard `kill()`/`terminate()` with `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`. On Linux the default `multiprocessing.Process` is the fork context's Process, not `SpawnProcess`, so the check is False for the actual flusher processes. The old process is then orphaned and `self.processes[process_index]` is overwritten with a new process while the old one keeps flushing the same shards, causing duplicate produces to buffered-segments, Redis contention, and process leaks. The same guard in `join` means hung spawn processes are never terminated.

findings.title: Restarting one flusher shard-group leaks the old worker and duplicates flushing
findings.body: `_ensure_processes_alive` calls `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)` to replace a dead/hung worker. For the `threading.Thread` test path there is no stop/kill at all, and for the process path the kill is skipped by the bad isinstance check. All workers also share a single global `stopped` flag, so there is no way to stop only the replaced worker. The old worker keeps running `SpanFlusher.main` on the same shards while the new worker starts, so two workers concurrently call `flush_segments`/`done_flush_segments` and `produce` for the same shards, duplicating Kafka messages and corrupting flush bookkeeping.

findings.title: Inconsistent metric tag shard vs shards breaks flusher dashboards
findings.body: `SpanFlusher.main` emits `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` and `spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes` with `tags={"shard": shard_tag}` but emits `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` with `tags={"shards": shard_tag}`. The singular vs plural tag name means the three timers for the same flusher cannot be correlated/grouped, breaking existing dashboards and alerts that filter on `shard`.
